title: Conjugacy of sections of a triangular group quotient with smooth diagonal quotient
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $F$, and closed subgroups have the meaning of [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $n\geq1$, let $B_n\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_{n,F}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group] be the group of invertible upper triangular matrices, and let $U_n\subseteq B_n$ be the subgroup with all diagonal entries $1$; these descriptions apply to points over every commutative $F$-algebra. Let $J\subseteq B_n$ be a closed subgroup, and put $V=J\cap U_n$, the scheme-theoretic intersection. Let $q:J\to D$ represent the fppf sheaf quotient $J/V$: the sheafification of $A\mapsto J(A)/V(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $F$-algebras. Assume that $D$ is smooth over $F$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For any two group-scheme homomorphisms $s_1,s_2:D\to J$ satisfying $q\circ s_i=\operatorname{id}_D$, there is $v\in V(F)$ such that $s_2=\operatorname{Int}(v)\circ s_1$ as morphisms of group schemes. Explicitly, for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$ and $d\in D(A)$, one has $(s_2)_A(d)=v_A(s_1)_A(d)v_A^{-1}$, where $v_A$ is obtained from $v$ by scalar extension. No smoothness hypothesis on $J$ or $V$, and no connectedness hypothesis, is imposed.

source.place: Summary 16.29(b), printed p.334, conjugacy of homomorphism sections with smooth multiplicative-type quotient; Theorem 16.27(a), printed p.333, requires the missing smoothness hypothesis on D (see report.md, Source error). Triangular realization: Proposition 16.2(c), printed p.325, and Theorem 16.21, printed p.330.

proof.text: For upper triangular matrices, $\delta(g)=(g_{11},\ldots,g_{nn})$ satisfies $\delta(gh)=\delta(g)\delta(h)$, and its scheme-theoretic kernel is $V$. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] to $\delta:J\to\mathbf G_m^n$. It represents the fppf quotient $J/V$ as a closed subgroup of $\mathbf G_m^n$. Its identification with the given $D$ is the unique one commuting with $q$, since both represent the same sheaf quotient. By [lem-sfb-split-torus-subgroups-diagonalizable], $D\simeq\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M$. For each pair $(i,j)$ let $\chi_{ij}:D\to\mathbf G_m$ be the restriction of $t_i/t_j$. Thus $\chi_{ij}(q(g))=g_{ii}/g_{jj}$ on every algebra. The assumed smoothness of $D$ is retained.

Use [lem-sfb-unitriangular-coordinate-filtration], writing $m=n(n-1)/2$, $C_r=(i_r,j_r)$ and $V_r=J\cap U^{(r)}$. These are subgroups normal in $J$, with $V_0=V$ and $V_m=1$. Restrict its coordinate homomorphism $p_r$ to $V_{r-1}$. By [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] it factors as $V_{r-1}\xrightarrow{a_r}N_r\hookrightarrow\mathbf G_a$, where $a_r$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented and has scheme-theoretic kernel $V_r$. The coordinate conjugation formula gives
$$a_r(gxg^{-1})=\chi_{i_rj_r}(q(g))a_r(x).$$
In particular, substituting $g=s_1(d)$ shows that $N_r$ is stable under the scalar character $\chi_{i_rj_r}$ of $D$: locally lift an $N_r$-point through the fppf quotient $a_r$, conjugate that lift by $s_1(d)$, and use the displayed formula. Membership in a closed subgroup descends under faithfully flat covers, since its defining equations vanish if they vanish after an injective faithfully flat algebra map.

Each $a\in N_r(F)$ lifts to $v\in V_{r-1}(F)$. Indeed, the faithfully flat surjective map $a_r$ supplied by [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] has nonempty fibre above $a$. This fibre is affine of finite type over $F$: its algebra is the quotient of the finitely generated coordinate algebra of $V_{r-1}$ by the equations $a_r=a$. A maximal ideal of this nonzero algebra gives a closed point. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] its residue field is $F$, giving the required $v$. This argument applies even when the fibre or $V_{r-1}$ is nonsmooth or nonreduced.

source.place: Theorem 16.27(a), p.333, lifting a rational point of a quotient; cf. 5.48, p.111.

proof.text:
For any homomorphism section $h:D\to J$, the morphism $c(d)=h(d)s_1(d)^{-1}$ lands in $V$, because its image under $q$ is $1$. Direct multiplication gives, as morphisms on $D\times D$,
$$c(dd')=c(d)\bigl(s_1(d)c(d')s_1(d)^{-1}\bigr).$$
Indeed $h(d)=c(d)s_1(d)$, and inserting this expression in $h(d)h(d')s_1(dd')^{-1}$ gives precisely the displayed formula. These identities hold on every algebra, not just on $F$-points.

source.place: Example 15.1, pp.302--303; opening observation in Theorem 16.27, p.333.

proof.text:
Induct on $r=0,\ldots,m$ with the claim that some $w_r\in V(F)$ makes $h_r=\operatorname{Int}(w_r^{-1})\circ s_2$ satisfy $c_r=h_rs_1^{-1}:D\to V_r$. For $r=0$ take $w_0=1$ and use step 4. Suppose the claim holds for $r-1$. The morphism $f_r=a_r\circ c_{r-1}:D\to N_r$ satisfies
$$f_r(dd')=f_r(d)+\chi_{i_rj_r}(d)f_r(d')$$
by step 4, the homomorphism property of $a_r$, and the scalar conjugation formula of [lem-sfb-unitriangular-coordinate-filtration]. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-diagonal-additive-crossed-vanishing]: step 1 supplies diagonalizability, smoothness is a hypothesis of the item, and step 2 supplies scalar stability. Obtain $a\in N_r(F)$ with $f_r(d)=a-\chi_{i_rj_r}(d)a$, and lift it to $v\in V_{r-1}(F)$ by step 3. Set $w_r=w_{r-1}v$. Then
$$c_r(d)=v^{-1}c_{r-1}(d)s_1(d)v s_1(d)^{-1},\qquad a_r(c_r(d))=-a+f_r(d)+\chi_{i_rj_r}(d)a=0.$$
All factors in $c_r$ lie in $V_{r-1}$, which is normal in $J$; the scheme-theoretic kernel description in step 2 therefore factors $c_r$ through $V_r$. This completes the induction with identities on every commutative $F$-algebra.

source.place: Theorem 16.27(a), p.333, successive removal of principal crossed homomorphisms; smooth-D scope of Summary 16.29(b), p.334.

proof.text: At $r=m$, $V_m=1$, so $c_m=1$ and $\operatorname{Int}(w_m^{-1})\circ s_2=s_1$. Hence $s_2=\operatorname{Int}(w_m)\circ s_1$. Taking $v=w_m\in V(F)$ proves the assertion and its formula after any scalar extension. If $n=1$, the filtration is empty and $V=1$, so the same argument says $s_2=s_1$. The proof never assumes $J$ or $V$ smooth, nor any group connected.

proof_origin.place: Theorems 16.21 and 16.27(a), pp.330,333; Summary 16.29(b), p.334. The same filtration induction is written in successive-coordinate form rather than quotient-by-last-term form.
